key_insight: SAGE-PINN encodes cylindrical axisymmetric geometry and conservation laws directly into a PINN to remove the axis singularity and model coupled flow–heat physics without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free surrogate for stenosed-artery and similar axisymmetric multiphysics CFD problems, reducing the need for case-specific tuning while preserving mass conservation.
method: Uses the parity-preserving variable s=r^2 and a modified stream-function to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly with boundary-fitted analytical ansätze.
Stabilizes training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, and Péclet/Richardson continuation.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element references for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, with mass conservation at round-off and central-range errors of 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-driven slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
